 CHINESE LEADER AT ASEAN SUMMIT. China's Premier Li Qiang gestures to Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. while Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung and Singapore's Prime Minister Lawrence Wong look on in a photo opportunity during the 29th ASEAN-China Summit as part of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in Manila on November 16, 2026. 
 TED ALJIBE/Pool via REUTERS 
 INFO 
 'We remain firmly committed to safeguarding multilateralism and promoting free trade and endeavor to make the pie bigger,' Chinese Premier Li Qiang says in remarks to ASEAN leaders in Manila 
 AT A GLANCE
 Chinese Premier Li Qiang praised the strong economic ties between China and ASEAN, highlighting over $1 trillion in trade and $500 billion in investment despite global trade challenges.
 As US President Donald Trump prepares to arrive in Manila, protests are expected against his administration's policies, while ASEAN leaders discuss regional cooperation and denuclearization efforts.
 This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors . 
 MANILA, Philippines – Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Monday, November 16, hailed what he called “truly extraordinary” achievements of China and Southeast Asia in the face of global trade restrictions, expressing Beijing’s commitment to free trade at a summit ahead of US President Donald Trump’s arrival.
 In remarks to leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations in Manila, Li said that at a time of growing unilateralism and protectionism and recurring geopolitical conflict, economic relations between China and ASEAN had only strengthened.
 “The past five years have been truly extraordinary, and the achievements we scored have not come easily,” he said, citing annual trade with the 11-member ASEAN last year of more than $1 trillion and cumulative two-way investment of more than $500 billion.
 “We remain firmly committed to safeguarding multilateralism and promoting free trade and endeavor to make the pie bigger,” he said.
 China is ASEAN’s biggest trading partner and a key source of investment, but the biggest economies of the bloc — which has a combined GDP of more than $3.9 trillion – are keen to expand ties with the United States amid trade and diplomatic uncertainty under the Trump administration.
 According to a readout of Li’s remarks by state news agency Xinhua, he said that in today’s turbulent world “it is all the more important for China and ASEAN to stand united, ward off interference, and work together.”
 Trump to face protests in Manila
 Trump is due to arrive in Manila on Tuesday, November 17, towards the end of the summit ahead of his trip to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen, where a trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin is scheduled.
 Anti-Trump protests are expected when he arrives in Manila, after four days of demonstrations and the burning of Trump effigies by leftist groups, students, and workers demanding an end to the Middle East war and the scrapping of the US-led Pax Silica initiative.
 In Manila, Trump will meet ASEAN leaders and attend his first meeting of the Quad group of Indo-Pacific powers — the US, Japan, Australia, and India — the first such gathering in two years.
 His predecessor Joe Biden saw the Quad as a signature foreign policy achievement and stressed the importance of maintaining it during his six meetings with the group.
 The Quad is widely considered an attempt to counterbalance China’s influence in the region, including by Beijing, although its members have said the grouping is not directed against any one country.
 UN ready to help any denuclearization move
 ASEAN held talks on Monday with the leaders of Australia, South Korea and the United Nations, whose Secretary-General Antonio Guterres reiterated calls for a ceasefire in Ukraine and for greater humanitarian access in war-torn Myanmar.
 Referring to trilateral talks planned in Shenzhen on Thursday, Guterres also said the UN was ready to fully engage on any denuclearization initiative between the United States, Russia and China, despite a lack of certainty about such an outcome.
 Trump has previously said he thought a denuclearization deal with Russia and China was possible. China’s Foreign Ministry on Monday said the trilateral talks would “promote world peace and stability”.
 “This is what we would like to see,” Guterres said about denuclearization. “It’s not yet guaranteed that we will get there.”
 South Korean President Lee Jae-myung on Monday proposed new initiatives on AI and creative industries to ASEAN and said negotiations to expand their free trade deal were progressing.
 “We must respond proactively to the changing global trade environment and move forward together towards an era of $300 billion in annual trade,” he said.
 The ASEAN leaders’ summit ended on Sunday without completing a protracted code of conduct with Beijing to try to manage disputes over the South China Sea, which ASEAN chair the Philippines had hoped could be wrapped up this year.
 ASEAN also resolved to continue its policy of excluding Myanmar’s leaders from its summits, but left the door open for a return if “sustained and concrete progress” on a peace plan agreed long ago with ASEAN can be demonstrated.
 The meeting also saw an apology from Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto to neighbouring Singapore and Malaysia over the impact of sustained transboundary haze from months of wildfires. – Rappler.com
